status: OUR ESTIMATE from public Solana data. Allegation by an analytics firm; not a finding about any person. Timing and funding links do not prove common ownership.

claim_summary.claimed: A caller's public wallet plus 3 side wallets bought before callouts and sold about 3 minutes later; 49 tokens; ~$125K total (~$45K trading + ~$80K callout rewards).
claim_summary.source: Analytics firm's X thread (Oct 2026) as quoted by news outlets; the thread itself could not be opened from this session.

sample.window_utc: 2026-08-12 to 2026-10-11 (claimed period, start of paid callout rewards to 2 days after the thread); joint trading by all three side wallets only from 2026-09-22
sample.wallets: 1 public + 3 side wallets (resolved from the 6-character prefixes the analytics firm published)
sample.selection: Slots where all three side wallets had a successful transaction (544) -> every 10th read (55) -> 44 distinct tokens -> first 9 kept + every 2nd of the remaining 35 -> 27 tokens rebuilt in full (25 with buys by both the public and side wallets)
sample.signatures_in_window: each side wallet had roughly 6,000-8,000 signatures in the window, 75-82% of them failed transactions
sample.data: Every trade parsed from transaction balances read from a public Solana RPC node

weighted_estimate_sep22_oct11.method: Each sampled token weighted by 1 / (chance it was picked): joint slots were read 1 in 10, so a token with k joint slots counts 10/k (capped at 1 chance), times 2 for tokens kept 1 in 2. 90% range from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of the 27 tokens.

pnl.note: PnL = SOL in minus SOL out per wallet per token, fees, tips and account rent included. USD uses an on-chain SOL/USDC price per day (median of 2-4 swap legs; 3 days interpolated from neighbours). Side-wallet PnL includes tokens the public wallet moved to them for free, so the group (public + sides) figure is the fair one.

links_anonymized: One side wallet was the first source of value for both other side wallets (SOL for one, USDC for the other).
The other first SOL funding came from two different one-off intermediary wallets (no shared funder at hop 1).
The public wallet sent tokens directly to the side wallets: in 9 of the 25 sampled tokens, and in one transaction to all three at once.
Side wallets sent USDC to the public wallet 6 times (about 2,700 USDC in total, late Sep to early Oct).
These links fit common control but do not prove who controls the wallets.

claim_vs_measured.claim: Public wallet belongs to the caller
claim_vs_measured.measured: The caller's public platform profile lists a wallet with the published prefix.

claim_vs_measured.claim: Public + 3 side wallets bought in the same second
claim_vs_measured.measured: Same block (same second) in 25 of 25 sampled tokens. A side wallet was earlier in the block in 23 of 25; all three side wallets were ahead in 11 of 25; the public wallet was first in 2 of 25.
Callout times are not on-chain and were not reachable.

claim_vs_measured.claim: Side wallets sold about 3 min after the callout (average)
claim_vs_measured.measured: Relative to the public buy: first side sell median 93 s, mean 165 s; SOL-weighted median 262 s; last side sell median 424 s.
About 199 tokens traded jointly by all three side wallets from Sep 22 to Oct 11 (90% range 151-252); which of them were callouts cannot be told from chain data.
Four wallets combined, weighted estimate for Sep 22 - Oct 11: about 460 SOL, about $55,000 (90% range $10,000-$118,000). Side wallets alone about $71,000; public wallet negative.
USDC credits to the public wallet from one daily mass-payout wallet, Sep 14 - Oct 9: about 55,000 USDC on 22 days; Aug 14 - Sep 13 not checked; payer not confirmed as the platform.
Not checkable for October 2026; the public profile count today differs and is not comparable in time.

claim_vs_measured.claim: Side wallets sold while the caller kept promoting
claim_vs_measured.measured: Posts are off-chain. On-chain, in some tokens the public wallet bought more while the side wallets were selling.

story_calibration.entry: All four wallets buy in one block (~0.4 s), side wallets usually a few positions ahead of the public wallet (median 7 transactions).
story_calibration.public_entry_price_premium: The public wallet paid a median ~9% more per token than the first side wallet in the same block (IQR ~8-15%).
story_calibration.exit: First side sell median ~1.5 min after the public buy (IQR ~20 s - 3 min); last side sell median ~7 min (IQR ~1-11 min); winners were sold in many small pieces (up to ~30 sells per wallet).
story_calibration.public_wallet_exit: The public wallet usually sold in the same block as the side wallets' final sell (median hold ~7 min).
story_calibration.pnl_shape: Group result per token: median about +0.6 SOL, IQR about -0.4 to +7 SOL; a few big winners (up to ~+30 SOL) carry the total. The public wallet lost on most tokens (profitable on 3 of 25).
story_calibration.token_age_example: Token age when the group bought, in the three charted examples: about 10 s, 70 s and 270 s after creation.
story_calibration.charted_examples: Peak after the public buy in the three charts: about 1.6x, 2.9x and 2.2x the public wallet's entry price; each ended below the public entry (lows about 0.53x, 0.40x and 0.57x within 30 min).
story_calibration.bots: Around these launches most transactions were failed or no-op bot attempts: in one 40-minute window, about 5,600 transactions touched the curve, about 1,500 succeeded and only about 480 actually traded.
story_calibration.public_wallet_behaviour: In the staged-exit example the public wallet added three more buys (at about +1, +5 and +9 min) while the side wallets were selling, then sold everything in the same block as the side wallets' last sell.

script_note: The claim figures above (token count, dollar totals) identify the real case. Do not put them on screen; the story uses fictional composites.
